description: Total min/max primitives over signed i64 values. This task is intentionally self-contained: do not depend on std/math/clamp.mm because that module is not guaranteed to exist in the current mumei checkout. Use std/core.mm's safe_narrow/min/max style as context, then emit independent atoms whose contracts stay in Z3's decidable integer fragment. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/math/min_max — verified min/max primitives'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/core.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only conditionals, comparisons, conjunction, disjunction, and integer constants already present in std/core.mm.
implementation_notes: Use direct if/else expressions rather than calling a missing std/math/clamp.mm module.
min2 body shape: if a <= b { a } else { b }.
max2 body shape: if a >= b { a } else { b }.
min3 may be expressed by nested comparisons or by inlining the min2 shape.

atoms.name: min2
atoms.description: Minimum of two i64 values. The contract proves both the order property and that the result is one of the inputs.
atoms.ensures: result <= a && result <= b && (result == a || result == b)

atoms.name: max2
atoms.description: Maximum of two i64 values. The contract proves both the order property and that the result is one of the inputs.
atoms.ensures: result >= a && result >= b && (result == a || result == b)

atoms.name: min3
atoms.description: Minimum of three i64 values. Keep the proof in linear integer arithmetic by using nested if/else comparisons only.
atoms.ensures: result <= a && result <= b && result <= c && (result == a || result == b || result == c)
